handbookNote: New Mexico's Revised Uniform Law on Notarial Acts (RULONA), NMSA 1978, Chapter 14, Article 14A, Sections 14-14A-1 to 14-14A-32 (enacted by Laws 2021, ch. 21, substantially amended by Laws 2023, ch. 110 / Senate Bill 246) plus New Mexico Secretary of State notary-commissions guidance -- batch 2 depth expansion: fills statutory gaps not covered in batch 1, including the full Section 14-14A-2 definitions (representative capacity, judicial officer, official notary seal variants, record, stamping device, etc.), the previously-untested interstate/federal/foreign-notarial-act provisions (Sections 9, 12, and 13, including apostilles and consular authentication), remaining certificate-mechanics detail in Sections 14-16 (timing rules, automatic-notarial-officer certificate content, stamp copy-ability), journal recordkeeping mechanics under Section 18(D)-(H) (lost/stolen journals, the attorney-notary journal exception, mandatory vs. optional transmission on death/resignation), commission-lifecycle and transition provisions in Sections 20-21 and 27 (dual-role commissioning, CLE credit, stamp grandfathering), the remaining Section 22 discipline grounds and the Section 26 rulemaking-authority provisions for both the secretary of state and the state ethics commission, remaining Section 24 prohibited-acts/advertising-disclaimer detail, Section 28 fee mechanics with worked calculation scenarios, and cross-cutting scenario/error-pattern questions applying identification, refusal, signing, and electronic/RON rules to new concrete fact patterns -- same $9.99 price tier as batch 1
